instructions: Start in a high plank. Lower your body until your chest is close to the floor, then press back up.
Lie on a bench. Unrack the bar, lower it to your mid-chest with control, then press to lockout.

Step 1: Set up a stability ball at an incline angle.
Step 2: Attach the cable handles to the high pulleys of a cable machine.
Step 3: Sit on the stability ball facing away from the machine, with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Step 4: Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Step 5: Lean forward slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Step 6: With a controlled motion, bring your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 7: Continue the motion until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Step 8: Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 9: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a stability ball at an incline angle.
Step 2: Attach the cable handles to the high pulleys of a cable machine.
Step 3: Sit on the stability ball facing away from the machine, with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Step 4: Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Step 5: Lean forward slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Step 6: With a controlled motion, bring your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 7: Continue the motion until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Step 8: Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 9: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Hold the handles of the cables with your palms facing down and your arms extended straight out to the sides.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, bring your hands together in front of your body, crossing them over each other.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position, keeping your arms extended.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with a wide grip and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Step 3: Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Grab the parallel bars with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Step 2: Bend your knees and cross your ankles.
Step 3: Lower your body by bending your arms until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Step 4: Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 2: Keep your arms straight and raise the barbell in front of you until it reaches shoulder height.
Step 3: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 4: Next, lower the barbell behind your head, keeping your arms straight.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then raise the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Engage your core and lower your body down towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Step 3: As you lower yourself, lean your body forward and lift your feet off the ground, balancing on your hands.
Step 4: Continue to lower your body until your chest is just above the ground.
Step 5: Push through your hands and extend your arms to lift your body back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Maintain a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Find a suspension trainer and adjust it to an appropriate height.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the anchor point and hold the handles with an overhand grip.
Step 3: Walk your feet forward, leaning your body forward until your weight is supported by the suspension trainer.
Step 4: Keep your body straight from head to heels, engage your core, and lower your chest towards the handles.
Step 5: Push through your chest and arms to return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm decline chest press
instructions:
Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest.
Step 2: Place your feet flat on the ground and keep your back pressed against the bench.
Step 3: Extend your arm and push the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, fully extending your elbow.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Adjust the smith machine to an incline position.
Step 2: Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Step 5: Raise the barbell up towards the ceiling, leading with your elbows.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach cables to both sides of a cable machine at chest height.
Step 2: Stand in the center of the machine with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and extend your arms out to the sides.
Step 4: Keep a slight bend in your elbows and maintain a slight forward lean.
Step 5: Engage your chest muscles and bring your arms forward in a sweeping motion.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the center, then slowly return your arms back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Step 2: Lie back on the bench and press the dumbbells up to the starting position, directly above your chest, with your arms extended.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 4: As you lower the dumbbells, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward at the bottom of the movement.
Step 5: Reverse the motion and bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles together at the top.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Find an elevated surface, such as a bench or step, and place your hands shoulder-width apart on the edge.
Step 2: Step your feet back, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Step 3: Lower your chest towards the edge of the surface, bending your elbows and keeping your body aligned.
Step 4: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 5: Jump off the edge of the surface, landing softly with your knees slightly bent.
Step 6: Repeat the push-up and depth jump for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Step 3: Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight.
Step 3: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 4: From the push-up position, pull your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight.
Step 5: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: roller seated single leg shoulder flexor depresor retractor
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Step 2: Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Step 3: Lean back slightly and engage your core muscles.
Step 4: Raise the roller up to shoulder level, keeping your arms straight.
Step 5: Slowly lower the roller back down to your thighs.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie down on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips and your feet secured.
Step 2: Hold the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Extend your arms above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the motion.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: roller seated shoulder flexor depresor retractor
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Step 2: Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Step 3: Lean forward slightly and roll the roller away from your body, extending your arms straight in front of you.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the roller back towards your body, bending your arms and bringing the roller back to your thighs.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a push-up position with your hands on the floor and your shins resting on the stability ball.
Step 2: Engage your core and lift your hips up towards the ceiling, rolling the ball towards your hands.
Step 3: Keep your legs straight and your body in a pike position, forming an inverted V shape.
Step 4: Bend your elbows and lower your upper body towards the floor, keeping your head in line with your hands.
Step 5: Push through your hands and extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: wide-grip chest dip on high parallel bars
instructions:
Step 1: Position yourself on the parallel bars with your arms fully extended and your body suspended in the air.
Step 2: Lean forward slightly and lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest is just above the bars.
Step 3: Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie down on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended straight up over your chest.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 4: As you lower the dumbbells, twist your wrists so that your palms face forward at the bottom of the movement.
Step 5: Reverse the motion and bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles at the top.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: band one arm twisting chest press
instructions:
Step 1: Attach the band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height.
Step 2: Stand with your side facing the anchor point and grab the band with one hand.
Step 3: Step away from the anchor point to create tension in the band.
Step 4: Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Step 5: Bring your hand holding the band across your body, towards the opposite shoulder.
Step 6: While maintaining tension in the band, push your hand forward and away from your body, extending your arm.
Step 7: Slowly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Step 8: Switch sides and repeat the exercise with the other hand.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 3: Once your chest is just above the ground, explosively push yourself up, lifting your hands off the ground.
Step 4: As you push up, quickly move your hands out to the sides and slightly forward, allowing your body to drop down towards the ground.
Step 5: Catch yourself with your hands in the wider position and immediately lower your chest towards the ground again.
Step 6: Repeat the push-up motion, dropping down and catching yourself with your hands in the narrower position.
Step 7: Continue alternating between the wider and narrower hand positions for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Step 2: Extend one arm straight out to the side, parallel to the ground.
Step 3: Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Step 4: Push back up to the starting position, using your chest muscles to lift your body.
Step 5: Repeat with the other arm extended.

Step 1: Stand facing a wall, about arm's length away.
Step 2: Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Step back with your feet, keeping them hip-width apart.
Step 4: Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Step 5: Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the wall, keeping your body straight.
Step 6: Pause for a moment, then push yourself back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by kneeling on the ground with your hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Step 2: Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, so that your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Step 3: Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Step 4: Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground, with your palms facing each other.
Step 3: Squeeze your chest muscles together as hard as you can, while keeping your arms straight.
Step 4: Hold this position for a few seconds, focusing on contracting your chest muscles.
Step 5: Release the squeeze and relax your chest muscles.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: barbell reverse grip incline bench press
instructions:
Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Step 6: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands on the kettlebells, shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 3: Push through your hands explosively, lifting your hands off the kettlebells and extending your arms fully.
Step 4: Land softly back on the kettlebells and immediately lower your chest back down for the next repetition.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and one hand placed slightly wider than the other.
Step 2: Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: As you lower yourself, shift your weight to one side and lift the opposite arm off the ground, extending it straight out to the side.
Step 4: Push through your chest and triceps to raise your body back up to the starting position, while simultaneously lowering your extended arm back to the ground.
Step 5: Repeat the movement, alternating the arm you extend with each repetition.

Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lower the barbell to your chest, keeping your elbows out to the sides.
Step 4: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your palms facing forward and your arms extended above your chest.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then push the dumbbells back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell lying one arm press v. 2
instructions:
Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your back supported and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing towards your feet.
Step 3: Extend your arm straight up towards the ceiling, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Step 4: Slowly lower the dumbbell down towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to a decline position.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the machine and grab the handle with one hand.
Step 3: Position yourself with your back against the decline bench and your arm extended straight in front of you.
Step 4: Bend your elbow and lower the handle towards your chest while keeping your upper arm stationary.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the handle back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and backrest angle on the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Step 2: Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Push the handles forward and away from your body until your arms are fully extended, but without locking your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly bend your elbows and lower the handles back towards your chest.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to a decline position.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Hold the handles with your palms facing forward and your arms extended straight out in front of you.
Step 4: Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a controlled motion.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: barbell reverse grip decline bench press
instructions:
Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with a reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Step 2: Hold the exercise ball with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Step 3: Slowly bring the exercise ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your chest muscles.
Step 4: Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Step 3: Push explosively off the ground, using your chest muscles to propel your upper body off the ground.
Step 4: Land softly with your hands back in the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: barbell wide reverse grip bench press
instructions:
Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with a wide reverse grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Step 4: Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in and your wrists straight.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your upper back is resting on the exercise ball.
Step 3: Extend your arm with the dumbbell straight up above your chest, palm facing inwards.
Step 4: Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, exhaling during the movement.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position, inhaling as you do so.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Position yourself on parallel bars with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Step 2: Lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are below your elbows.
Step 3: Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a weight plate in front of your chest with both hands.
Step 2: Keep your elbows slightly bent and your palms facing each other.
Step 3: Press the weight plate straight out in front of you, fully extending your arms.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly bring the weight plate back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your thigh.
Step 2: Lie back on the bench and position the dumbbell at shoulder level, palm facing forward.
Step 3: Press the dumbbell upward and slightly inward, extending your arm fully.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Place the stability ball on the ground and position yourself facing down with your hands on the ball, shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Extend your legs straight out behind you, balancing on your toes.
Step 3: Engage your core and lower your chest towards the ball by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Position yourself between two parallel bars with your arms extended and supporting your body weight.
Step 2: Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Step 3: Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Step 3: Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the dip bars to a height that allows you to comfortably grip them.
Step 2: Stand between the bars and place your hands on each bar, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Jump up and straighten your arms, supporting your body weight on the bars.
Step 4: Bend your knees and cross your ankles behind you.
Step 5: Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping your chest up and your shoulders down.
Step 6: Continue lowering until your shoulders are below your elbows or until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 7: Push through your palms and extend your elbows to raise your body back up to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm incline chest press
instructions:
Step 1: Adjust the incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the ground.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an overhand grip, resting it on your shoulder.
Step 4: Push the dumbbell up and away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Lean back on the bench and use your thighs to help raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Step 3: Once at shoulder height, rotate your wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward.
Step 4: Push the dumbbells up with your chest and shoulders, extending your arms fully.
Step 5: Lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating arms.

exerciseName: assisted seated pectoralis major stretch with stability ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Step 2: Hold a stability ball with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Step 3: Slowly lower the stability ball towards your chest, feeling a stretch in your pectoral muscles.
Step 4: Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Place the bosu ball on the ground with the flat side facing up.
Step 2: Position yourself in a push-up position with your hands on the outer edges of the bosu ball.
Step 3: Engage your core and lower your body down towards the bosu ball by bending your elbows.
Step 4: Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by lying on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, with your palms facing towards your feet and your arms extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Step 3: Lower one kettlebell down towards your shoulder while keeping the other kettlebell extended straight up.
Step 4: Press the lowered kettlebell back up to the starting position while simultaneously lowering the other kettlebell down towards your shoulder.
Step 5: Continue alternating the press motion with each kettlebell for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to a decline position.
Step 2: Sit on the decline bench facing the cable machine.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position them at chest level.
Step 4: Keep your feet flat on the ground and your back firmly against the bench.
Step 5: Exhale and push the handles away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, squeezing your chest muscles.
Step 7: Inhale and slowly return the handles back to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by lying flat on your back on a mat or bench.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight out to the sides, perpendicular to your body.
Step 3: Engage your core and lift both legs off the ground, keeping them together and straight.
Step 4: Slowly lower your legs to one side, aiming to touch the ground with your feet while maintaining control.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then use your core to lift your legs back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat the movement, this time lowering your legs to the opposite side.
Step 7: Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Sit on the bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the ground.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Step 4: Start with your arms fully extended, perpendicular to the ground.
Step 5: Lower the dumbbells slowly to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees at a 90-degree angle.
Step 2: Hold the cable handles at chest height with your palms facing down and your elbows bent.
Step 3: Engage your core and press the cable handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly release the tension and bring the cable handles back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: kettlebell extended range one arm press on floor
instructions:
Step 1: Start by lying on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a kettlebell in one hand, with your palm facing towards your feet.
Step 3: Extend your arm straight up towards the ceiling, keeping your elbow locked and your wrist straight.
Step 4: Slowly lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline one arm fly on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Step 2: Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbell with your arm extended straight up over your chest, palm facing inwards.
Step 4: Slowly lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when your arm is parallel to the ground.
Step 6: Engage your chest muscles to bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exerciseName: cable one arm decline chest fly
instructions:
Step 1: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and set the bench to a decline angle.
Step 2: Lie down on the bench with your head towards the machine and grab the handle with your right hand.
Step 3: Extend your arm straight up above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Step 4: With a controlled motion, lower your arm out to the side until your hand is in line with your shoulder.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then reverse the motion and bring your arm back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left arm and repeat the exercise.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley position.
Step 2: Sit on an incline bench facing away from the cable machine.
Step 3: Grasp the handle with one hand and bring it up to shoulder height.
Step 4: Position your feet firmly on the ground and maintain a stable position.
Step 5: Press the handle forward and upward, extending your arm fully.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handle back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline one arm press on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand, feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbell at shoulder height with your palm facing forward.
Step 4: Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Step 4: Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows slightly flared out.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest, then push it back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Place your hands on the edge of a box or elevated surface, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet, creating a straight line from your head to your heels.
Step 3: Lower your chest towards the box by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with a pronated grip and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Step 3: Exhale and push the handles forward, bringing them together in front of your chest.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, squeezing your chest muscles.
Step 5: Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, allowing your chest muscles to stretch.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Lie back on the bench and position the dumbbells at shoulder level with your palms facing each other.
Step 3: Press the dumbbells up and away from your body until your arms are fully extended.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down.
Step 2: Rest the dumbbells on your thighs and lean back onto the bench.
Step 3: Use your thighs to help raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, then rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing forward.
Step 4: Exhale and slowly raise the dumbbells above your head, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Step 2: Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported by the ball.
Step 3: Extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
Step 4: Bend your elbows slightly and lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then reverse the movement and squeeze your chest muscles as you bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline fly on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Sit on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the incline bench.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then squeeze your chest muscles to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing a cable machine.
Step 2: Grasp the handle with one hand and step back to create tension on the cable.
Step 3: Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 4: Extend your arm out to the side, parallel to the ground, with a slight bend in your elbow.
Step 5: Slowly bring your arm back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exerciseName: smith wide grip decline bench press
instructions:
Step 1: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Step 2: Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with a wide grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows pointed outwards.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Step 6: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: medicine ball chest push from 3 point stance
instructions:
Step 1: Start in a 3 point stance with one hand on the medicine ball and the other hand on the ground.
Step 2: Extend your legs and position your body in a straight line.
Step 3: Lower your chest towards the ground while keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Push the medicine ball away from your body, extending your arm fully.
Step 5: Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Place your hands on the ground slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with your feet elevated on a stable surface.
Step 2: Keep your body in a straight line from head to toe, engaging your core muscles.
Step 3: Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Step 4: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and your head lower than your hips.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other and your arms extended above your chest.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Step 4: Press the dumbbells back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to chest height and attach the handles.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and step forward to create tension in the cables.
Step 4: Position your feet firmly on the ground and engage your core.
Step 5: Bend your elbows and bring your hands to shoulder level, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 6: Push the handles forward, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Step 7: Pause for a moment, then slowly reverse the movement, bringing your hands back to shoulder level.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to chest level.
Step 2: Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Step 3: Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the bar and lower it towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the bar touches your chest.
Step 6: Push the bar back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell pullover hip extension on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and the dumbbell resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your arms straight and maintaining control.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: While keeping your arms extended, lift your hips off the ground, squeezing your glutes and engaging your core.
Step 7: Lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold the resistance band handles in each hand, with your palms facing down and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Extend your arms forward, pushing the resistance band away from your chest.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Step 4: Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Step 6: Push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to chest level.
Step 2: Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Step back and position yourself with a slight bend in your knees.
Step 5: Keep your chest up and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 6: Lower the bar towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 7: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the bar back up to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the decline bench to the desired angle.
Step 2: Lie down on the bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing a wall, about arm's length away.
Step 2: Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Step back a few feet, keeping your body straight and your feet hip-width apart.
Step 4: Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the wall, keeping your body in a straight line.
Step 5: Push back up to the starting position, straightening your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline press on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Step 2: Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Step 4: Press the dumbbells upward, extending your arms fully.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Place the bosu ball on the ground with the flat side facing up.
Step 2: Position yourself in a push-up position with your hands on the outer edges of the bosu ball.
Step 3: Engage your core and lower your body down towards the bosu ball by bending your elbows.
Step 4: Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and cable handles to a comfortable position.
Step 2: Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Step 3: Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip at shoulder height.
Step 4: Push the handles forward and away from your body, extending your arms fully.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then slowly bring the handles back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold the kettlebell in one hand with your palm facing towards your feet and your arm extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Step 3: Slowly lower the kettlebell towards your chest by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Step 4: Pause for a moment when the kettlebell is just above your chest, then push it back up to the starting position by extending your elbow.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Adjust the bench to a 30-45 degree incline.
Step 2: Sit on the bench with your back flat against the pad and feet firmly on the ground.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your upper chest, keeping your elbows slightly tucked in.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Step 2: Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your body in a straight line.
Step 3: Pause for a moment when your chest is just above the ground, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine to a low position and attach the handles.
Step 2: Sit on an incline bench with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Step 4: Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides in a controlled motion.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the fully extended position, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Place your hands on the bench slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Position your feet on the ground, hip-width apart.
Step 4: Lower your chest towards the bench, keeping your elbows tucked in.
Step 5: As you lower, retract your shoulder blades, squeezing your scapulae together.
Step 6: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Step 3: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and handlebar position to a comfortable level.
Step 2: Sit on the ergometer with your back straight and feet on the pedals.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with your hands and position your arms at a 90-degree angle.
Step 4: Start pedaling with your hands, pushing and pulling the handles in a controlled motion.
Step 5: Continue pedaling for the desired duration or number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Lower your chest towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 3: Once your chest is just above the ground, quickly drop your knees to the ground.
Step 4: Push yourself back up to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lower the barbell slowly towards your neck, keeping your elbows pointed outwards.
Step 4: Pause for a moment when the barbell is just above your neck.
Step 5: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Step 2: Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Step 3: As you lower, rotate your body to the left, extending your left arm straight out to the side.
Step 4: Push back up to the starting position, while rotating your body to the center.
Step 5: Repeat the push-up, this time rotating your body to the right and extending your right arm out to the side.
Step 6: Continue alternating sides with each repetition.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the band handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Extend your arms fully, pushing the bands away from your chest.
Step 4: Slowly lower the bands back down to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Lower your body by bending your elbows and retracting your shoulder blades, as if you are trying to squeeze a pencil between them.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Step 2: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Let the dumbbell hang straight down in front of you, with your arm fully extended.
Step 4: Pull the dumbbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Step 5: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Step 6: Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a towel with one hand.
Step 2: Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Extend your arm fully, allowing the towel to hang in front of you.
Step 4: Pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the towel back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 3: Engaging your back muscles, lift the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: lever one arm bent over row
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a barbell with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your head up.
Step 3: Let the barbell hang in front of you with your arms fully extended.
Step 4: Pull the barbell up towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 5: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Step 6: Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: cable reverse-grip straight back seated high row
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on the seat facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the floor.
Step 2: Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward from your hips.
Step 4: Pull the cable towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the peak of the contraction, then slowly release the cable back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a decline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended towards the floor.
Step 4: Keeping your arms straight, raise your shoulders towards your ears as high as possible.
Step 5: Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on the stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 2: Slowly walk your feet forward, rolling the ball down your back until your lower back is resting on the ball.
Step 3: Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Step 4: Engage your core and slowly lower your upper body towards the ground, allowing your lower back to stretch over the ball.
Step 5: Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a handle to a cable machine at waist height.
Step 2: Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the handle with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 4: Step back to create tension on the cable, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Step 5: Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your palms to face upwards as you do so.
Step 6: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Step 7: Slowly release the handle back to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and sit on the bench with your chest against the incline.
Step 3: Extend your arms fully, allowing the dumbbells to hang straight down from your shoulders.
Step 4: Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing a pull-up bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Reach up and grab the bar with an underhand grip, with one hand gripping the bar and the other hand holding your wrist for support.
Step 3: Hang from the bar with your arm fully extended, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Step 4: Pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbow and squeezing your back muscles.
Step 5: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.

Step 1: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Step 3: As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Step 4: Continue pulling yourself up until your chest reaches the bar, then pause for a moment.
Step 5: Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired assistance level.
Step 2: Stand on the foot platform and grip the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your chest up and shoulders back, engage your core, and slightly bend your knees.
Step 4: Pull your body up by flexing your elbows and driving your elbows down towards your sides.
Step 5: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on the machine with your feet flat on the footrests and your knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and lean slightly forward, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a kettlebell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Step 2: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Pull the kettlebells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Engage your core and use a swinging motion to generate momentum.
Step 3: As you swing forward, pull your chest towards the bar, using your lats and biceps to initiate the movement.
Step 4: Continue the upward motion until your chest reaches the bar, then transition into a dip position by pushing down on the bar and extending your arms.
Step 5: Lower yourself back down to the starting position by bending your arms and controlling the descent.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Step 2: Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, lower the barbell behind your head in a controlled manner until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a towel in front of you with your palms facing down.
Step 2: Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and your chest up.
Step 3: As you lower into the squat, simultaneously pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the squat, then slowly return to the starting position while extending your arms.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself facing the machine.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your back straight.
Step 3: Pull the handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the peak of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by sitting on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Step 2: Place the roller perpendicular to your body, just below your glutes.
Step 3: Slowly roll your body backwards, allowing the roller to move up your back.
Step 4: Continue rolling until the roller reaches your upper back.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then slowly roll back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: medicine ball catch and overhead throw
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball in both hands at chest level.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Step 3: Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Step 4: Explosively extend your hips and legs, while simultaneously throwing the medicine ball overhead.
Step 5: Release the ball at the top of the movement and catch it on the way down.
Step 6: Lower your body back into the squat position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing towards you and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Step 3: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended and your toes resting on top of the stability ball.
Step 2: Place your hands on the ground, shoulder-width apart, and engage your core muscles.
Step 3: Keeping your legs straight, slowly lift them off the ground, using your lower back and glutes to raise them as high as possible.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a bar at waist height or use a suspension trainer.
Step 2: Stand facing the bar or suspension trainer, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grab the bar or handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Lean back, keeping your body straight and your heels on the ground.
Step 5: Pull your chest towards the bar or handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a single handle to a high pulley cable machine.
Step 2: Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the handle with an overhand grip and extend your arm fully.
Step 4: Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 5: Pull the handle down towards your side while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your lat muscle.
Step 7: Slowly release the handle back to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Step 9: Switch sides and repeat the exercise with the other arm.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a towel in front of you with both hands.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Pull the towel towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell side plank with rear fly
instructions:
Step 1: Start by lying on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other.
Step 2: Place your forearm on the ground directly below your shoulder, keeping your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, with your arm extended straight down towards the ground.
Step 4: Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your head to your heels.
Step 5: While maintaining the side plank position, lift the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Step 1: Position yourself under a bar or a sturdy horizontal surface that is at chest height.
Step 2: Grab the bar or surface with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Hang with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Step 4: Pull your chest towards the bar or surface by squeezing your shoulder blades together and bending your elbows.
Step 5: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar or surface.
Step 6: Lower yourself back down to the starting position with control.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Grab the pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Step 3: Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Step 4: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Hang from a pull-up bar with a narrow parallel grip, palms facing towards you.
Step 2: Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 3: Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Step 4: Pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Kneel on the ground with your knees hip-width apart and your toes pointing back.
Step 2: Extend your arms overhead and interlace your fingers.
Step 3: Keeping your back straight, slowly lean to the right side, feeling a stretch in your left lat muscle.
Step 4: Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat the stretch on the left side, leaning to the left and feeling a stretch in your right lat muscle.
Step 6: Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, parallel to the ground.
Step 3: Rotate your torso to the right, keeping your arms extended and your back straight.
Step 4: As you rotate, extend your right arm forward and your left arm back, mimicking the motion of drawing a bowstring.
Step 5: Hold the position for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat the motion, this time rotating your torso to the left and extending your left arm forward and your right arm back.
Step 7: Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Step 2: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor, with your elbows slightly bent.
Step 4: Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a cable handle to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Step 2: Grasp the handle with your left hand and step away from the machine, extending your arm fully.
Step 3: Position your feet shoulder-width apart, with your knees slightly bent.
Step 4: Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 5: Pull the handle towards your body, rotating your torso to the right as you do so.
Step 6: Squeeze your back muscles at the end of the movement.
Step 7: Slowly return to the starting position, keeping tension on the cable.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and perform with your right hand.

exerciseName: band fixed back close grip pulldown
instructions:
Step 1: Attach the band to a fixed point above you, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam.
Step 2: Sit down on a bench or chair facing the band, with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent.
Step 3: Grasp the band with a close grip, palms facing towards you.
Step 4: Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Step 5: Pull the band down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, feeling the contraction in your lats.
Step 7: Slowly release the band back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: barbell reverse grip bent over row
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up, until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Pull the barbell towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your knees under the pads and your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Sit upright with your chest out and shoulders back, maintaining a slight arch in your lower back.
Step 4: Pull the handles down towards your chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Engage your core and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Step 3: Pull your body up towards the bar until your chin is above the bar.
Step 4: Lower your body back down to the starting position with control.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell reverse grip incline bench two arm row
instructions:
Step 1: Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.
Step 2: Sit on the bench with your chest against the backrest and your feet flat on the ground.
Step 3: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Step 4: Lean forward and let your arms hang straight down, fully extended.
Step 5: Pull the dumbbells up towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height settings.
Step 2: Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Engage your lats and biceps, and pull yourself up towards the handles.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your back muscles.
Step 6: Slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the cable machine so that the pulldown bar is at a height above your head.
Step 2: Sit down on the seat and grab the pulldown bar with an underhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and lean back slightly.
Step 4: Pull the bar down towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, then slowly release the bar back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie down on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips and your feet secured.
Step 2: Hold a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Step 3: Lower the barbell behind your head in a controlled manner, keeping your arms slightly bent.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position by contracting your lats.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a barbell on the floor and lie face down on a bench with your chest just off the edge.
Step 2: Reach down and grab the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: With your legs straight and feet on the ground, lift the barbell off the floor by extending your arms.
Step 4: Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Lower the barbell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand in front of a pull-up bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Reach up and grab the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Step 4: Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: exercise ball back extension with hands behind head
instructions:
Step 1: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it with your hips resting on the ball.
Step 2: Position your feet against a wall or other stable surface for support.
Step 3: Cross your arms behind your head, with your hands touching the back of your head.
Step 4: Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, extending your back until your body forms a straight line from your head to your hips.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: ez bar lying bent arms pullover
instructions:
Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Step 2: Hold the EZ barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing away from you) and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Extend your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then return the barbell to the starting position by reversing the arc motion.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outwards.
Step 2: Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended downwards.
