Step 3: Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Drive through your heels and explosively extend your hips and knees, pulling the kettlebell up towards your chin.
Step 5: As you pull the kettlebell up, keep your elbows high and wide, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: exercise ball back extension with arms extended
instructions:
Step 1: Place the stability ball on the ground and lie face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall for stability.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight out in front of you, with your palms facing down.
Step 3: Engage your core and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, keeping your back straight and your neck in line with your spine.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your bottom arm extended straight overhead.
Step 2: Bend your top knee and place your foot on the ground in front of your bottom leg.
Step 3: Reach your top arm over your head and grab onto something stable, like a wall or a piece of furniture.
Step 4: Slowly lift your bottom leg off the ground, keeping it straight, until you feel a stretch in your side.
Step 5: Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly lower your leg back down.
Step 6: Repeat on the other side.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Grasp a bar or handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Step 4: Pull the bar or handles towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement.
Step 6: Slowly release and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Bend forward at the hips while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Step 3: Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Pull the barbell towards your lower chest by retracting your shoulder blades and squeezing your back muscles.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat and handles of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Step 2: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and grasp the handles with an overhand grip.
Step 3: Keep your arms slightly bent and your core engaged.
Step 4: Slowly pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your lats.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a v-bar attachment to a cable machine at chest height.
Step 2: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the v-bar with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 4: Take a step back to create tension in the cable.
Step 5: Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 6: Pull the v-bar towards your torso by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Step 7: As you pull, twist your torso to one side, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 8: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your upper back.
Step 9: Slowly release the tension and return to the starting position, untwisting your torso.
Step 10: Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the twisting direction with each rep.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding onto a sturdy object or suspension trainer with your arms extended.
Step 2: Lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and your knees behind your toes.
Step 3: From the squat position, pull your body up towards the object or suspension trainer, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your head at one end and your feet on the floor.
Step 2: Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width grip and extend your arms straight above your chest.
Step 3: Lower the barbell behind your head while keeping your arms slightly bent.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height settings.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Hang with your arms fully extended and your feet off the ground.
Step 4: Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the handles, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 5: Continue pulling until your chin is above the handles.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to fit your body size and range of motion.
Step 2: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet secured.
Step 3: Place your hands on the handles or grip bars.
Step 4: Engage your core and slowly lean forward, allowing your back to round slightly.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom position, feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Step 6: Using your back muscles, slowly raise your torso back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: smith reverse grip bent over row
instructions:
Step 1: Set up the smith machine with the bar at hip height.
Step 2: Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 5: Pull the bar towards your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the height of the smith machine bar to waist level.
Step 2: Stand facing the smith machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Grasp the bar with one hand using an overhand grip, with your palm facing down.
Step 5: Keep your elbow close to your body and pull the bar towards your waist, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Stand facing a high bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Reach up and grab the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Step 4: Engage your lats and biceps to pull your chest up towards the bar, leading with your sternum.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a bar at waist height on a Smith machine or use a suspension trainer.
Step 2: Stand facing the bar or suspension trainer and grab it with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Walk your feet forward, leaning back until your body is at a slight angle.
Step 4: Keep your body straight and pull your chest up towards the bar or handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder level, palm facing forward.
Step 2: Press the dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended overhead.
Step 3: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Hold the cable handle with your arm extended in front of you, parallel to the ground.
Step 3: Keep your elbow slightly bent and your shoulder blades pulled back.
Step 4: Slowly rotate your arm outward, away from your body, while keeping your elbow in the same position.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie on your side on a flat bench with your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent 90 degrees.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in your hand with your palm facing down.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arm against your side, slowly rotate your forearm upward as far as possible.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Raise the cable handle in front of you, keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down.
Step 4: Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Step 2: Press one kettlebell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Step 3: Lower the kettlebell back to shoulder height.
Step 4: Repeat with the other arm.
Step 5: Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a D-handle to a low pulley cable machine and lie face down on a flat bench.
Step 2: Grasp the D-handle with each hand, palms facing down, and extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, raise them out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Step 2: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Step 3: Rotate your arms externally, bringing the dumbbells up towards your head while keeping your elbows in the same position.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Step 3: Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Rotate your arms so that your palms are facing downwards.
Step 5: Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit on it with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Step 2: Lean forward and let your arms hang straight down, perpendicular to the floor.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, raise them out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a 'T' shape with your body.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Step 2: Raise the dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Step 3: Engage your core and keep your back straight as you walk forward, maintaining the dumbbell overhead.
Step 4: Continue walking for the desired distance or time.
Step 5: Switch hands and repeat the exercise.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Step 3: Raise your arms out to the sides, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, until they are parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: cable kneeling rear delt row (with rope) (male)
instructions:
Step 1: Attach a rope handle to a low cable pulley and kneel down facing the machine.
Step 2: Grasp the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and extend your arms fully in front of you.
Step 3: Keeping your back straight and core engaged, pull the rope towards your body by retracting your shoulder blades.
Step 4: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement and hold for a brief pause.
Step 5: Slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Step 3: Raise the dumbbells to your sides with a slight bend in your elbows, until your arms are parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: barbell standing close grip military press
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly closer than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Lift the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 3: Press the barbell overhead, extending your arms fully.
Step 4: Lower the barbell back to shoulder height.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the band under your feet.
Step 2: Hold the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you.
Step 3: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Pull the band towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly release the tension and return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell seated bent arm lateral raise
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Keeping your elbows bent, raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Step 3: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Next, raise your arms in front of you until they are parallel to the ground, again keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline one arm lateral raise
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh.
Step 2: Lean forward and position your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Step 3: Raise the dumbbell to the side, keeping your arm slightly bent and your palm facing down.
Step 4: Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the floor.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Step 3: Raise the dumbbells in front of you, with your palms facing down, until they are at shoulder level.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Step 3: Press the kettlebell overhead in a straight line, fully extending your arm.
Step 4: As you press the kettlebell overhead, simultaneously dip your knees and quickly straighten them to generate momentum.
Step 5: As the kettlebell reaches its highest point, quickly drop underneath it by bending your knees and hips.
Step 6: Catch the kettlebell with a slight bend in your knees and hips, and your arm fully extended overhead.
Step 7: Stand up straight, fully extending your knees and hips, and stabilize the kettlebell overhead.
Step 8: Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position by bending your knees and hips, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and backrest of the leverage machine to a comfortable position.
Step 2: Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the floor.
Step 3: Grasp the handles of the machine with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Push the handles upward and forward until your arms are fully extended, but not locked.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Extend your arms straight down in front of you, palms facing each other.
Step 4: Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Step 2: Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.
Step 3: Press one dumbbell up overhead, fully extending your arm.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbell back down to shoulder height.
Step 5: Repeat with the other arm.
Step 6: Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Step 3: Raise the cable handle in front of you, keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down.
Step 4: Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell lying one arm deltoid rear
instructions:
Step 1: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing inwards.
Step 2: Extend your arm straight down towards the floor, keeping it close to your body.
Step 3: Raise your arm up and back, squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height.
Step 2: Press one kettlebell overhead while keeping the other kettlebell at shoulder height.
Step 3: Lower the pressed kettlebell back to shoulder height while simultaneously pressing the other kettlebell overhead.
Step 4: Continue alternating the pressing motion, creating a seesaw-like movement.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a D-handle to each low pulley cable and stand in the middle of the cable crossover machine.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and take a step forward, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Bend your knees slightly and lean forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your abs engaged.
Step 4: With your arms extended out to the sides and slightly bent at the elbows, exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the cables back and upward in a reverse fly motion.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell in front of your shoulders with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Press the barbell overhead, fully extending your arms.
Step 3: Lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Lower into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Step 3: As you reach the bottom of the squat, explosively drive through your heels to stand up, simultaneously pressing the barbell overhead.
Step 4: Lower the barbell back to shoulder height as you lower back into the squat position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hold the cable attachment with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 3: Pull the cable attachment straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Slowly lower the cable attachment back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Step 2: Press one dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Step 3: Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder level.
Step 4: Repeat with the other arm.
Step 5: Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step 2: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the ground, forming a T shape with your body.
Step 3: Pause for a moment, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Let the barbell hang in front of your thighs, arms fully extended.
Step 3: Keeping your back straight, exhale and lift the barbell straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Grasp the cable handles with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight in front of you.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, slowly raise them out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Raise the barbell out to the sides, keeping your arms straight, until they are parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at shoulder level.
Step 2: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Step 3: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and lift them off the supports, extending your arms fully.
Step 4: Lower the handles down to shoulder level, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Step 5: Press the handles up overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to shoulder level.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and engage your core.
Step 3: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Step 4: Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and arms extended down by your sides.
Step 3: Keeping your arms straight, raise one dumbbell in front of you until it is parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat with the other arm.
Step 6: Alternate between arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Let the barbell hang in front of your thighs, arms fully extended.
Step 3: Keeping your back straight and core engaged, exhale and lift the barbell straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your body.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 3: Raise the dumbbell to the side, keeping your arm straight and your palm facing down.
Step 4: Continue lifting until your arm is parallel to the ground.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing down.
Step 2: Keeping your core engaged and your elbows slightly bent, press the dumbbells up and overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Step 3: Rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing forward.
Step 4: Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your wrists back as you do so.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your back straight and your core engaged as you pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Step 5: Slowly release the handles back to the starting position and repeat.

exerciseName: kettlebell one arm military press to the side
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height.
Step 2: Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Step 3: Press the kettlebell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the top.
Step 5: Slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position and repeat, then switch sides.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell between your legs.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips.
Step 3: Explosively extend your hips and knees to swing the kettlebell upward.
Step 4: Rotate your hand and punch the kettlebell overhead, fully extending your arm.
Step 5: Lower the kettlebell back down and repeat.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Step 2: Keep your back straight and core engaged.
Step 3: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the top.
Step 5: Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart holding the band in front of your thighs.
Step 2: Keep your arms straight and lift them upward forming a Y shape.
Step 3: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Step 4: Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with back support holding dumbbells at shoulder level with palms facing your body.
Step 2: Press the dumbbells upward while rotating your palms forward.
Step 3: Fully extend your arms overhead.
Step 4: Pause briefly at the top.
Step 5: Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat.

Step 1: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Extend one arm across your chest.
Step 3: Use the opposite hand to gently pull the arm closer to your body.
Step 4: Hold the stretch for 15 to 30 seconds.
Step 5: Switch sides and repeat.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Step 2: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Step 3: Lower the bar to shoulder height.
Step 4: Press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Step 5: Pause briefly, then slowly lower the bar back down and repeat.

exerciseName: barbell decline close grip to skull press
instructions:
Step 1: Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet and hold a barbell with a close grip.
Step 2: Lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Step 3: Pause for a moment, then extend your arms to press the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Step 3: Allow the kettlebells to hang straight down in front of your body.
Step 4: In one fluid motion, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders.
Step 5: As the kettlebells rise, pull them up towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows high and out to the sides.
Step 6: Catch the kettlebells at shoulder height, with your palms facing inward and your elbows pointing forward.
Step 7: Lower the kettlebells back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Grasp the cable handle with an underhand grip, palm facing down.
Step 3: Keep your elbow close to your side and slowly curl your forearm up towards your shoulder.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward, and arms fully extended.
Step 2: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 3: Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 4: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed close together, directly under your shoulders.
Step 2: Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Step 3: Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the band with both hands, palms facing down.
Step 2: Extend your arms straight out to the sides, keeping them parallel to the ground.
Step 3: Slowly bend your elbows and bring your hands towards your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly extend your arms back out to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment at chest height.
Step 2: Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cable.
Step 3: Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Step 4: Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Step 5: Start with your arm fully extended and perpendicular to the floor.
Step 6: Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and push the bar down until your arm is fully extended.
Step 7: Pause for a moment, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Step 2: Rest your upper arms on your thighs, allowing the dumbbells to hang down.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell seated biceps curl to shoulder press
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and arms fully extended.
Step 3: Keeping your elbows close to your sides, curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Step 4: Once your forearms are vertical, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing forward.
Step 5: Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Step 6: Lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position by reversing the movement.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
Step 2: Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
Step 3: This will be your starting position.
Step 4: Now, while holding your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 5: Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 6: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 7: Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the handles towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale as you slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Find an open space with enough room to perform a handstand.
Step 2: Place your hands on the ground shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Step 3: Kick your legs up towards the wall, using your core and shoulders to maintain balance.
Step 4: Once in a handstand position, engage your triceps to support your body weight.
Step 5: Hold the handstand for as long as you can maintain balance.
Step 6: To come down, slowly lower your legs back to the ground.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold the ez barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Raise the barbell overhead, fully extending your arms.
Step 4: Keeping your upper arms stationary, lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then raise the barbell back to the starting position by extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Lower the barbell towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm reverse preacher curl
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your arm extended over the edge of the bench, holding a dumbbell with an underhand grip.
Step 2: Lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is fully extended.
Step 3: Curl the dumbbell back up towards your shoulder, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Step 4: Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso.
Step 2: Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
Step 3: This will be your starting position.
Step 4: Now, keeping the upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 5: Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 6: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 7: Then, inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 8: Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a rope handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Step 2: Lie down on a flat bench facing up, with your head towards the cable machine.
Step 3: Grasp the rope handle with both hands, palms facing each other, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.
Step 4: Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the rope handle towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: cable rope lying on floor tricep extension
instructions:
Step 1: Attach a rope to a cable machine and set it to the lowest position.
Step 2: Lie on the floor facing up, with your head towards the cable machine.
Step 3: Hold the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and extend your arms straight up towards the ceiling.
Step 4: Keep your upper arms stationary and slowly lower the rope towards your forehead, bending your elbows.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Hold the cable handle with your right hand and bring your arm up so that your upper arm is parallel to the ground and your elbow is bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Keep your upper arm stationary and extend your forearm backward, fully straightening your arm.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat with your left arm.
Step 6: Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: cable rope high pulley overhead tricep extension
instructions:
Step 1: Attach a rope to a high pulley and adjust the weight accordingly.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the pulley machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing down, and bring your hands above your head.
Step 4: Keep your upper arms close to your head and perpendicular to the floor.
Step 5: Slowly lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Step 6: Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell seated revers grip concentration curl
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up.
Step 2: Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands close together.
Step 2: Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Step 3: Exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Step 4: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale as you slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline one arm hammer press on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand.
Step 2: Walk your feet forward and roll your body down until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbell with your palm facing inward and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 4: Press the dumbbell up towards the ceiling, straightening your arm.
Step 5: Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Kneel down on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Step 2: Place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.
Step 3: Extend your legs straight behind you, balancing on your toes and hands, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Step 4: Bend your elbows and lower your upper body towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a v-bar attachment to the cable machine at the highest setting.
Step 2: Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the v-bar with an overhand grip, palms facing down, and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Step 5: Engage your triceps and exhale as you push the v-bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your triceps.
Step 7: Inhale as you slowly return the v-bar to the starting position, maintaining control.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand facing a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Hold the cable handle with your right hand and step back to create tension in the cable.
Step 3: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 4: Keep your upper arm close to your body and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 5: Extend your forearm backward, straightening your arm fully.
Step 6: Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exerciseName: ez-barbell standing wide grip biceps curl
instructions:
Step 1: Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ez barbell with an underhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Step 3: Curl the barbell up towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 3: Extend your arms straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
Step 2: Keep your elbows close to your torso and rotate your palms to face forward.
Step 3: Curl the dumbbells up to your shoulders while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Step 4: At the top of the movement, rotate your wrists so that your palms are facing away from your body.
Step 5: Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your palms back to facing your body.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell lying one arm supinated triceps extension
instructions:
Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with an underhand grip, and extend your arm straight up above your shoulder.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arm stationary, slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then extend your arm back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Adjust the machine to your desired weight and height.
Step 2: Kneel down on the pad facing the machine, with your hands gripping the handles.
Step 3: Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight and close to the machine.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell kneeling bicep curl exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Kneel on the floor with an exercise ball in front of you.
Step 2: Place your elbows on top of the exercise ball, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbells while contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 5: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 6: Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell bicep curl with stork stance
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Step 2: Extend one leg behind you, balancing on the toes of that foot.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Continue to raise the weights until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 5: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 6: Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

exerciseName: dumbbell seated alternate hammer curl on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms fully extended.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder while keeping your palm facing your body.
Step 4: Continue to raise the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Step 5: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 6: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Step 8: Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip, palms facing away from you.
Step 3: Extend your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbells down towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 5: As you lower the dumbbells, twist your wrists so that your palms face towards you at the bottom of the movement.
Step 6: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then reverse the movement by pressing the dumbbells back up to the starting position.
Step 7: As you press the dumbbells up, twist your wrists back to the starting position with palms facing away from you.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm seated hammer curl
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Step 3: Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Step 4: Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Step 6: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Step 1: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Step 2: Keep your upper arms close to your body and your elbows tucked in.
Step 3: Slowly curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your wrists straight.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a bench with your hands gripping the edge of the bench, fingers pointing forward.
Step 2: Slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.
Step 3: Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your back close to the bench.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the pad.
Step 2: Grasp the handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and keep your elbows close to your sides.
Step 3: Exhale and curl the handles upward, contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell over bench one arm neutral wrist curl
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm extended over the bench, palm facing up.
Step 2: Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder, keeping your wrist in a neutral position.
Step 3: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exerciseName: ez barbell close grip preacher curl
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a preacher curl bench and place your upper arms on the pad, gripping the ez barbell with an underhand grip.
Step 2: Rest your triceps on the pad and fully extend your arms, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Slowly curl the barbell towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Step 5: Lower the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.
Step 2: Using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.
Step 3: Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position.
Step 4: As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells to your side until they are about level with your chest.
Step 5: As you exhale, use your triceps to lift the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.
Step 2: Slide your hips forward off the bench and straighten your legs, keeping your heels on the ground.
Step 3: Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your back close to the bench.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your hands to straighten your arms and lift your body back up to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.
Step 2: Grasp the ez barbell with a close grip, hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward.
Step 3: Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Step 4: Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Step 5: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Step 6: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Set up a barbell on a power rack at chest height.
Step 2: Stand facing the barbell and position yourself underneath it, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step 4: Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it directly above your chest, with your arms fully extended.
Step 5: Lower the barbell down towards your chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body.
Step 6: Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.
Step 7: Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Step 8: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm concentration curl (on stability ball)
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the ground and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm extended down towards the floor.
Step 3: Rest your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee.
Step 4: Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder while contracting your biceps.
Step 5: Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.

exerciseName: dumbbell alternating seated bicep curl on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl one dumbbell while rotating your forearm until your palm is facing your shoulder.
Step 4: Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat the curl with the other arm.
Step 6: Continue alternating curls for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Attach a rope to a cable machine at a high position.
Step 2: Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 3: Grasp the rope with both hands, palms facing each other, and bring your hands above your head.
Step 4: Keep your upper arms close to your head and your elbows pointing forward.
Step 5: Slowly lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows.
Step 6: Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your arms extended over the edge, holding a barbell with an underhand grip.
Step 2: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 3: Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Step 4: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 5: Inhale and slowly begin to lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell tricep kickback with stork stance
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Step 2: Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.
Step 3: Bring your right elbow up to your side, keeping it bent at a 90-degree angle.
Step 4: Extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps.
Step 5: Pause for a moment, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 6: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exerciseName: dumbbell incline hammer press on exercise ball
instructions:
Step 1: Sit on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Step 2: Walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball.
Step 3: Hold the dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows bent and pointing out to the sides.
Step 4: Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward, keeping your palms facing each other.
Step 5: Extend your arms fully, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Step 6: Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Stand or sit upright with your back straight.
Step 2: Extend one arm overhead, bending it at the elbow.
Step 3: Place your opposite hand on the bent elbow and gently pull it towards your head.
Step 4: Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch in your triceps.
Step 5: Release the stretch and repeat on the other arm.

Step 1: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.
Step 2: Hold a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the ground.
Step 4: Pause for a moment, then contract your triceps to bring the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Step 1: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Step 2: Rest your upper arms on the bench, allowing your elbows to hang down and your palms to face forward.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.
Step 4: Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Step 5: Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.
Step 6: Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Step 7: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exerciseName: dumbbell one arm reverse spider curl
instructions:
Step 1: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down and arm fully extended.
Step 2: Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by flexing your elbow.
Step 3: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Step 4: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

exerciseName: band one arm overhead biceps curl
instructions:
Step 1: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place one end of the band under your foot.
Step 2: Hold the other end of the band with your arm fully extended overhead, palm facing forward.
Step 3: Keeping your upper arm stationary, curl your forearm towards your shoulder, squeezing your biceps.
Step 4: Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your forearm back to the starting position.

exerciseName: cable one arm reverse preacher curl
instructions:

exerciseName: dumbbell alternate biceps curl (with arm blaster)
